portal.paletteNote: Settled 2026-08-09, and derived from BetterTago's OWN delivered mark: brandColor is the emblem's deep green and anchors primary-700; accentColor is the mark's sun and anchors accent-400. It stays DELIBERATELY INDEPENDENT of the municipality's own visual identity — visual similarity to official material would imply an endorsement this project does not have. Do not derive these from tago.gov.ph, and do not use the municipal seal anywhere without written permission. Stated rather than left to be found: the mark's channels are abstracted from municipal motifs, so painting a whole site from it amplifies that derivation from a logo to a site. That belongs in the conversation with the municipality, and it is not settled here.

STILL OPEN, and recorded rather than implied: the national issuance that SET this classification was not retrieved, so the figure is the municipality's own statement about itself and carries no issuance date. population.label: Philippine Statistics Authority — PSGC record for Tago, Surigao del Sur
population.note: The 2024 census count for the whole municipality. V1 — CORROBORATED INDIRECT, and it must not be read as anything stronger. The primary record is the national statistics authority's own PSGC/census release at https://psa.gov.ph/classification/psgc/barangays/1606818000; that URL was requested again on 2026-08-10 and answered HTTP 403 to an automated request, as it has on every previous attempt. The figure below was therefore reached through the English Wikipedia article on Tago (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tago,_Surigao_del_Sur), which attributes it to that release. The tertiary path is named here rather than hidden: a person opening the PSGC page in a browser and recording what it says promotes this to V3, and that is the single cheapest outstanding task on this record.

landAreaKm2.label: Tago, Surigao del Sur — tertiary encyclopaedia record, infobox
landAreaKm2.note: ⚠️ PUBLISHED BY INSTRUCTION 2026-08-10, and the reader is owed the whole story rather than the number. The source gives TWO land areas for Tago and reconciles neither: 253.28 km² in its infobox and 343.52 km² in its body text, a 36% difference, re-read the same day and both still present. The value published here is the infobox one, and the selection is reasoned rather than a coin toss: the body's figure is the one its own stale arithmetic depends on — the density it prints, 86 persons per km², is reproduced exactly by 343.52 km² against the 2000 census, so that paragraph is a quarter-century old. Against the 2024 count neither area yields 86, and the density figure is rejected outright at every level. V1 — CORROBORATED INDIRECT. The primary record is a national land-area or cadastral release and it is NOT in hand; obtaining one is what promotes or corrects this, and it may well correct it.

emergency.note: Six agencies, read from a hotline post on the municipality's own official Facebook page, published 2026-08-10. Cited at V3 — the municipality publishing a number on its own channel is the municipality's own published record, which is what V3 means here. CITED TO THE PAGE, NOT THE POST, by instruction: the permalink to the specific post was available and was deliberately not used. The trade is real and is recorded rather than glossed — a page URL keeps working and is the channel a resident would think to check, but it does not pin the exact post these were read from, so checkedAt carries more of the weight. HISTORY, kept because it explains the shape of this record rather than being tidied away: four sweeps (the official site, the provincial site and two national police directories) are recorded under sourcesChecked and every one came back empty or unretrievable. That is why this field carried a settled position for months that the surface would render the absence rather than a number — it was the honest state at the time, and it changed because a source turned up, not because the standard moved. NOTE ON SCOPE: two of the six — the Coast Guard station and the Red Cross — are provincial or national bodies rather than municipal ones. They are listed because they serve Tago and a resident in an emergency needs them, which is different from substituting a provincial number FOR a missing municipal one; that substitution is still forbidden.

lgu.psgc.note: The national statistics authority publishes this municipality's PSGC record at psa.gov.ph/classification/psgc/barangays/1606818000. Checked 2026-08-09, re-attempted the same day for the barangay directory, and re-attempted a THIRD time on 2026-08-09 for the statistics baseline: the host answers HTTP 403 to an automated request every time, as does psa.gov.ph itself and every /classification/ and /statistics/ path tried. It is not behind a login and robots.txt permits it — closing this needs a person opening that URL in a browser and recording the code with the date they read it. Three attempts, all machine-refused, is the reason CONT-210 is recorded blocked rather than skipped. NOT A CHANNEL: an aggregator site answered 200 on the same sweep and was deliberately NOT READ — this project did not check what it carries, because a figure it cannot trace to the authority that published it is unusable either way. Recorded so the refusal is a decision on the record rather than an absence. RE-ATTEMPTED 2026-08-10 with the same result: HTTP 403. The population, census year and barangay count were closed at V1 through the tertiary path instead; this entry stays open because the PSGC CODE itself, and the per-barangay urban/rural classification, are on that page and nowhere else. FOURTH ATTEMPT 2026-08-10, specifically for the barangay-level urban/rural classification: the response is a Cloudflare interstitial ('Just a moment...', a JavaScript challenge), confirmed by reading the response body rather than only the status code — this is not a simple bot-header block that a different request might clear, and no automated fetch can complete it. The aggregator surveyed this time (philatlas.com) was READ rather than skipped, on the reasoning that its population tables are transparently PSA-derived and worth checking for this one field: its barangay table carries five population columns and NO classification column at all, so the earlier 'not a channel' decision did not need to be revisited — the data is simply not there to trace. The per-barangay classification remains obtainable only by a person opening the PSGC page in a browser.

contact.project.email.note: The only entry here that is not about the municipality. The correction channel is the public repository's issue tracker — live and linked from every page — but it needs a free account on a code-hosting site, which is a real barrier for exactly the resident most likely to spot a wrong fee at a counter. Closing this needs an address that exists and someone reading it; it needs no code, because the footer link is already null-guarded.
